symptom: In a disposable Linux synthetic test, a pinned root FD survived real-directory ancestor replacement, but a later-opened final-directory FD referred to the replacement. A writer and reader sharing that late FD consistently published and read the decoy's valid single-link JSON, not the previously authorized original. A control comparing the final FD with a simulated pre-authorized directory identity denied before publication. This is not a production incident or evidence of an authenticated authority.
lesson: Reader/writer agreement on a shared final-directory FD proves object consistency only after that FD is acquired; it does not authenticate how the final FD was bootstrapped from a pinned root with mutable child names. A deterministic preauthorized-final-object mismatch can be denied before publication, but pathname-derived metadata and a one-time comparison are not an independently authenticated durable trust anchor.
guardrail: Do not equate a pinned root FD, openat2 traversal restrictions, or self-consistent FD-relative read/write with authorized publisher identity. Require an independently reviewed final-directory bootstrap and lifecycle; reject demonstrated identity mismatch before publication; preserve fail-closed behavior across later rename/mount races. Do not treat st_dev/st_ino alone as cryptographic provenance or stable reachability. No automatic recovery, production integration, scoring, N2 activation, Current BUY, LINE, public publishing or private raw evidence.
